# Solar cell (photovoltaic cell) (`solar_cell`)

<!-- generated by scripts/build_techtree.py from techtree/core/electricity.yaml — do not edit -->

- Category: Electricity & electronics (`electricity`)
- Deps: helped by semiconductors_transistor, semiconductor_purification, quantum_mechanics, practical_batteries
- Core idea: Light absorbed in a semiconductor frees electrons and holes; the built-in field of a p-n junction lying just under the surface pulls them apart before they recombine, so the lit cell drives a current through an outside circuit. Make it from a thin slice of single-crystal silicon with a very shallow diffused layer of the opposite type on the sunny side (the first cells were n-type silicon with boron diffused in), a metal grid on the front and full metal on the back. Each cell gives about 0.5 volt whatever its size, the current grows with area and light, and cells are joined in series. The first such cells turned 6 per cent of sunlight into electricity, against under 1 per cent for selenium; full sunlight delivers about 1 kW per square metre.
- Pitfalls:
  - Confusing it with the photoelectric cell in a vacuum tube or with a solar boiler; no heat engine and no emission into vacuum is involved
  - A junction too deep below the surface: the light is absorbed before it reaches the junction and the carriers recombine
  - Promising cheap power soon; in the 1950s a watt of cells cost hundreds of dollars and the first real market was satellites
  - Forgetting that a shiny silicon surface reflects about a third of the light unless it is given an anti-reflection coating
- History: europe: 1839 – Edmond Becquerel finds a light-driven current in an electrolytic cell (Paris); 1873 Willoughby Smith, selenium conducts better in light; 1876 Adams and Day, a current from lit selenium; americas: 1883 – Fritts's selenium cells with gold film, about 1 per cent efficient (New York); 1940 Ohl's light-sensitive silicon junction; April 1954 silicon solar cell of Chapin, Fuller and Pearson (Bell Labs), 6 per cent; 1958 Vanguard 1 satellite powered by solar cells
- Read:
  - D. M. Chapin, C. S. Fuller & G. L. Pearson, A New Silicon p-n Junction Photocell for Converting Solar Radiation into Electrical Power, Journal of Applied Physics 25 (1954)
  - John Perlin, From Space to Earth: The Story of Solar Electricity (1999)
